newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia again threatens quota on EU textile imports.
newsitem.headline: Russia again threatens quota on EU textile imports.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Thursday once again raised the prospect that Moscow may slap import quotas on European textiles,
"If the question of textiles is not worked out, we will put a quota on the European market on all textiles coming into Russia," he told the cabinet.

A carryover accord between Moscow and the European Commission expired in April and has not been replaced with a new deal. Under the April agreement, the commission gave duty-free status to five Russian product types and increased quota limits on 34 other Russian products types by 15 percent.

Moscow has often threatened to slap quotas on European textile imports. Chernomyrdin met EU trade officials last week in Brussels to discuss increasingly prickly trade issues but no substantial agreements were reached.
Total Russian textile exports to the European Union were 26,789 tonnes in 1995, the last year for which data was immediately available.
Russia's imports of EU textiles were valued at $750 million a year, while its exports of textiles to Europe were limited to $140 million a year, Interfax news agency said.
The European Union is Russia's largest trading partner but it also has more restrictions than other countries against Russia, whom it has accused of dumping products at low prices.
